MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  BUDGET STUDY SESSION
  JUNE 14, 2022

1.  ALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 5:35 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely
via teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council
Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498, 2499, 2503, 2505 and 2507 due to the
continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result
of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG
Led by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

3.  ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present:  Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Accountant Fernando Estrada
  Administrative Assistant Carol Corea

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

NONE

5.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 BUDGET STUDY SESSION

City Manager Grammer provided a brief overview of the estimated year-end results for the
current fiscal year and the proposed budget for the next fiscal year, 2022-2023. The budget
can be described as fiscally conservative and stable. He thanked the Budget Subcommittee,
which includes Council Member Schmitz and Council Member Stegura and thanked
Accountant Estrada and Administrative Services Director Whitehead for their work in preparing
the budget.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a summary of the staff report (as per the
agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA asked if the city has the flexibility to invest out of state since
inflation bonds are paying 9.6% locked in for 5-years. Director Whitehead stated that the city
has some flexibility but cannot lock-in for 5-years due to the need for liquidity; the city has one
CD that is locked in for 6-months.

City Manager Grammer noted that it has been City Council’s policy to use “extraordinary”
revenue for a one-time use or for extraordinary purposes; this does not go into operating
expenditures.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if anything over the baseline of $900K is considered
“extraordinary.” City Manager Grammer stated that this would be anything in the $1.8M - $2.0M
range.

CITY COUNCIL BUDGET STUDY SESSION MINUTES  1
JUNE 14, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ asked about the increase in Business License Penalties, which
went from $9K to $25K. Director Whitehead stated that it could have been from vendors not
paying business license fees in the prior year; but cannot say for sure. He also confirmed that
it did not have to do with any change in collecting procedures.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF asked about the “need to be used by” time limit for Park Facilities
Fees. Director Whitehead stated that this is typically five years. City Manager Grammer stated
that funds that the City is awarded, such as Measure R, Prop C, Measure M are used as they
are received.

In response to a question by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, Director Whitehead confirmed
that the funds that can be held are invested until they can be used.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ asked if the water costs have included a penalty for usage or
if it is the straight rate. Director Whitehead stated that it is the straight rate per gallon. Assistant
City Manager Davis stated that there have been some water main breaks that have caused
more usage; however, the rates have also increased.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked about water saving technology. Assistant City
Manager Davis stated that MWD had a program that the city did not quality for. City Manager
Grammer stated that the city is working with Cal Water on a drip replacement program at City
Hall and Highridge Park.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that the budget identifies $293K for Highridge Park.
Assistant City Manager Davis stated that this is mostly for the turf replacement project.

Director Whitehead noted a change to the Computer Network Upgrade budget to move a
Planning/Building & Safety application to the Cloud. The one-time cost for the upgrade is
approximately $15K. The Computer Network Upgrade budget will be increased by $15K.

Accountant Estrada provided an explanation on the General Fund and Special Fund items.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked about Prop A – Fourth District Grant of which
$44,529 has not been reimbursed. Assistant City Manager Davis stated that staff is actively
trying to identify which project this funded and if these funds are still available, then staff will
submit for reimbursement.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked about the $510K allocated to Capital Projects
Replacement. Director Whitehead stated that this is for improvements to the City Hall and
Chamber building exterior.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked about the PERS UAL and if in addition to the audit,
should the history be included in the budget message. City Manager Grammer agreed that
since the public is likely to review the budget, this is a good suggestion.

In response to a question by MAYOR ZERUNYAN, Director Whitehead stated that the
contingency reserve and the emergency reserve under the Unassigned category must be 25%
of expenditures anything above 25% is put under the Assigned category.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if personnel costs could be added to the Emergency
Management category. Director Whitehead stated that he will look into it for next year. City
Manager Grammer stated this is worth looking into, considering the amount of work
Management Analyst Slawson has done in emergency management.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired about breaking out the School Resources Officer
from the Public Safety category for transparency of the amount the city is contributing. Director
Whitehead said that he will look into adding a new account code and will update the description
in the budget activity detail page.

In a question by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Director Whitehead stated that Life
Insurance is for all full-time employees and confirmed that it is based on the employee’s salary.
The policy is two times the salary with a maximum of $200K.

CITY COUNCIL BUDGET STUDY SESSION MINUTES  2
JUNE 14, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked about Contractual Services under Stormwater. City
Manager Grammer stated that Measure W is for stormwater mitigation measures. Director
Wahba stated that some is being used in a few areas, some of which includes: the drywell
siting study, low impact requirements for the Nature Center, and the project at Rolling Hills
Road to address stormwater runoff.

THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECTED STAFF TO PREPARE THE FINAL BUDGET FOR
PRESENTATION AND PUBLIC HEARING ON JUNE 28, 2022.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 6:45 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting to the Regular City Council meeting 7:00
p.m.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carol Corea on behalf of  Frank V. Zerunyan
Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL BUDGET STUDY SESSION MINUTES  3
JUNE 14, 2022
